list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: Terbium(III) selenium–lanthanide-bridged tetra-vacant Dawson-like selenotungstate aggregate

measurements.conditions: Solid state, room temperature; emission monitored at 544 nm
measurements.name: Photoluminescence average decay time

properties.summary: Visible solid-state photoluminescence with characteristic Tb(III) emissions; the measured average decay time at 544 nm was 11.64 ms.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The tetrameric polyoxoanion is formed from four tetra-vacant Dawson-like [Se2W14O52] fragments and a 24-nuclear Se–Tb–W oxo-cluster. It can be viewed as two equivalent dimeric sandwich subunits, each containing two Dawson-like fragments around a [Tb4W4Se4O22(H2O)5] cluster, joined by double W–O–Tb linkers.

synthesis.ph: 4.5 reported as the condition giving highest yields; a pH range of 4.3–4.8 was reported as beneficial
synthesis.procedure: One-pot assembly reaction of sodium tungstate dihydrate, sodium selenite, and lanthanide nitrate under acidic aqueous conditions, with dimethylamine hydrochloride and K+ used as structure-stabilizing/counter-cation components. The article reports that changing the lanthanide nitrate amount from 0.12 to 0.17 g afforded compounds 1–6, with highest yields at about 0.15 g; the reported Se/W molar-ratio range was 1.40–2.50, with the highest yields at 2.00.

reagents.amount: 0.12–0.17 g; about 0.15 g gave highest yields
reagents.name: terbium(III) nitrate hexahydrate
